answers.reasoning: (A) evaporates fits 'altogether' — things vanish; (B) free fits 'from stodgy fame'; (C) enhances fits 'reinforces and __'
restores fits 'art __ its visibility'; bury fits 'may well __ it' (negative); significant fits 'because it reinforces'
accumulates fits 'imitations and clichés'; inherent fits 'qualities already __ in it'; strange fits 'more strange, newly strange'
①evaporates OK, ②suited OK, ③free OK. ④trivial contradicts 'reinforces and enhances' — should be significant
①granted OK (take for granted), ②elevate contradicts 'bury' context — bury means to cover up, elevate is opposite. ③enhances OK, ④foreign OK
①visibility OK, ②precisely OK. ③possesses is opposite of lacks — bad text lacks strangeness, not possesses it. ④reaches OK
The blank is 'it __ altogether' — something domesticated vanishes/evaporates. evaporates fits perfectly
'the mode of __' — translation is not a makeshift but the mode of existence. existence fits
'__ of that work free it from its stodgy fame' — translations free the work from fame
domesticated means tamed, made familiar. tamed is the closest synonym
stodgy means dull, boring, old-fashioned. dull is closest synonym
inherent means innate, built-in, natural. innate is the closest synonym
approachable means easy to approach, friendly. forbidding (unapproachable, intimidating) is the opposite
makeshift means temporary, improvised. permanent is the opposite
(A) 'a great work of literature' — work = 작품. (B) 'system didn't work' — work = 작동하다
'bring back to former condition; return to previous state' = restore
Subject position needs a noun. translate(verb) → translation(noun)
'native ___' needs a noun. strange(adj) → strangeness(noun)
Berman's term: 'lacks native strangeness' — native strangeness is the answer
'we just __ until art restores its visibility' — take it for granted
